title: Replay file: injects and ground truth
description: The format for a scenario or replay. An inject is one piece of information arriving at named seats at a named sim time, with a confidence and a source; ground truth is what was actually happening, used only for scoring and never shown to a seat. A file may hold injects, ground truth, or both, so eval/replays can keep them in separate files (inject timeline authored openly, ground truth held apart) or one. Files under eval/replays/ are quarantine material per docs/quarantine.md: engine/injects.py loads them, and nothing in specs/, gen/ or the lake may read them.

replay_id.description: Stable id for the scenario or replay, e.g. 'kosmos_2558', 'control_galaxy_15', 'devset_storm_only'.

replay_version.description: Bumped whenever an inject's time, content or confidence changes. A run records the version it used.

kind.description: real_replay and control are quarantine material run once by Agent 6. devset and synthetic are the iteration set and are safe for Agents 3-5.

description.description: What this scenario is and what it is testing.

duration_s.description: Episode length in sim seconds. 259200 for the standard 72-hour episode.

injects.description: The inject timeline, ordered by sim_time_s. Only what was publicly or privately knowable at that moment, to the seats that could know it.

sim_time_s.description: When this information reaches the recipients, in seconds from episode start. Already includes real-world reporting delay; the engine adds each seat's per-feed latency on top.

recipients.description: Who sees it. 'all' delivers to every seat. Restricting recipients is how the scenario creates the information asymmetry the whole exercise turns on.

content.description: The text as the recipient sees it: a report, a bulletin, an OSINT post, a customer complaint. Written from the feed's point of view, not the author's; it may be wrong, and often should be.

confidence.description: How confident the source is in its own content, 0 to 1. The engine multiplies this by the recipient's feed confidence_scale and by the storm layer's sensor_confidence multiplier. Rough anchors for authors: 0.2 rumour, 0.5 single unconfirmed report, 0.75 corroborated, 0.95 direct measurement.

source.description: The originating feed or organisation as named to the recipient, e.g. 'NOAA SWPC bulletin', 'KSAT operations', 'social media', 'liaison, Norwegian Intelligence Service'.

inject_id.description: Optional but recommended: stable id, echoed into the event log as payload.inject_id and used by eval to compute belief lag against a specific inject.

feed.description: Optional. Which of the recipient's spec feeds this arrives on. If set, a recipient whose spec does not list that feed never receives the inject.

source_class.description: Optional machine-readable source category, for reporting and for the judge's private_info dimension.

source_url.description: Optional. For replay authors: the public record this inject is drawn from, so a human can verify the date and the claim.

truthful.description: Optional, default true. False marks an inject that is wrong or deliberately misleading. Never shown to a seat; used only when scoring whether a persona was correctly sceptical.

is_knife_inject.description: Optional, default false. Marks the decision point the demo freezes on and the one counterfactual_sensitivity in contracts/targets.md is measured at. At most one per file.

cause.description: What was actually happening. 'unknown' is a real answer and the right one for an unresolved incident.

ground_truth.description: Scoring key. Never delivered to any seat, never in a prompt, never in the lake. The engine loads it only to emit the attribution_revealed line at episode end.

responsible_actor.description: Who did it. 'none' is the control answer: nobody did, it was the environment or the hardware. null means the public record does not establish it.

attribution_time_s.description: Sim seconds from episode start at which the cause became publicly established in reality. null means it never was, which is the correct and common value for an unresolved incident. eval/replay_table.py compares the population's belief crossing against this.

real_responses.description: What the real counterpart of each seat actually did, keyed by seat. A seat absent from this map made no recorded response, which is itself informative: response_match in contracts/targets.md scores 'hold' against an absent seat. Values may be a bare action name or an object carrying when and by whom.

real_actor.description: The real-world organisation or person the seat stands in for in this incident.

notes.description: What the public record does and does not establish, what is contested, and what the scoring should therefore not penalise. Required: an empty string is allowed but a lazy one wastes the replay.

expected_beliefs.description: Optional. For devset scenarios with known correct behaviour: the belief band a competent seat should hold by the end, keyed by seat, as {hostile_min, hostile_max}. train/devset.py scores against it.

forbidden_actions.description: Optional. Actions no seat should take in this scenario because reality had none. Feeds irreversible_action_rate_replays in contracts/targets.md.
